p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The paradigm of global public health is undergoing a critical transition, shifting focus from reactive, hospital-centric disease treatments to proactive, systemic disease prevention. While high-tech tertiary care facilities command the lion’s share of political prestige and healthcare funding, they function as reactive safety nets that treat illnesses only after they have caused severe bodily and financial harm. This hyper-focus on curative medicine ignores the rising tide of non-communicable diseases (NCDs)—such as cardiovascular illnesses, type-2 diabetes, and chronic respiratory conditions—which are heavily driven by commercial factors, including ultra-processed foods, environmental pollution, and urban designs that discourage physical activity. Addressing this epidemiological shift requires robust structural interventions, including heavy taxes on unhealthy commodities, strict regulations on food marketing, and major investments in walkable urban spaces. Furthermore, true disease prevention demands strengthening primary healthcare clinics, which act as the essential front line for early diagnosis and community health education. Public health must be re-framed not as the clinical management of sickness, but as the structural preservation of collective wellness.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The phenomenon of language extinction presents a critical challenge to cultural diversity worldwide. Linguistic diversity encapsulates unique worldviews, traditions, and historical narratives intertwined within speech and expression. However, globalization and homogenizing forces of dominant languages continue to marginalize minority tongues, risking irreparable loss. Scholars argue that language preservation is not only about safeguarding words but also about protecting collective identities and knowledge systems rooted in indigenous languages. Revival efforts thus emphasize community participation, digital documentation, and intergenerational transmission to reinvigorate endangered languages. Despite advancements, practical challenges abound, including insufficient resources, political neglect, and urban migration patterns that detach younger generations from native idioms. Ultimately, the urgency lies in not just recognizing linguistic loss but mobilizing multifaceted strategies to preserve the tapestry of human expression for posterity.

questions.q: The author argues that tertiary care facilities are overemphasized because they:
opts: Function as reactive safety nets that treat illnesses only after harm has occurred.
Focus exclusively on eliminating non-communicable diseases through taxation.
Prioritize systemic disease prevention over expensive clinical interventions.
Are structurally embedded within primary public health education clinics.
questions.why: Detail: they 'treat illnesses only after they have caused severe bodily and financial harm'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the text, non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are heavily driven by:
opts: Commercial and structural factors like ultra-processed foods and pollution.
Genetic mutations that escape early diagnosis.
A lack of high-tech tertiary care facilities in urban centers.
The over-taxation of basic consumer commodities.
questions.why: Detail: 'heavily driven by commercial factors, including ultra-processed foods, environmental pollution'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following is mentioned as a structural intervention to combat the rise of NCDs?
opts: Banning community health education in primary clinics.
Taxes on unhealthy commodities and investment in walkable urban spaces.
Shifting primary care funding into high-tech hospital construction.
Reducing regulation of ultra-processed food marketing.
questions.why: Detail: both are listed among the 'robust structural interventions'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The passage highlights primary healthcare clinics as critical because they:
opts: Command the largest share of political prestige and funding.
Focus on high-tech surgery for advanced heart disease.
Manage the marketing campaigns of food companies.
Serve as the front line for early diagnosis and community health education.

questions.q: The main idea of the passage is that public health strategy must pivot toward:

Deregulating food industries to promote economic growth.

questions.q: Choose the correct conditional sentence:
opts: If he left earlier, he would have caught the train.
If he would have left earlier, he would have caught the train.
If he had left earlier, he would have caught the train.
If he had left earlier, he would catch the train yesterday.
questions.why: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle. Never 'would have' in the if-clause. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Find the error: “The list of approved candidates are displayed on the notice board.”
questions.why: The subject is 'list' (singular): 'is displayed'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “Someone has stolen my bag.”
questions.why: Present perfect passive: has been + past participle; drop 'someone'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “You ______ wear a helmet; it is the law.”
questions.why: 'Must' expresses obligation. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “He is accused ______ taking a bribe.”
questions.why: 'Accused of'; but 'charged with'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Mamlatdar is to Taluka as Collector is to:
questions.why: A Mamlatdar heads the revenue administration of a taluka; a Collector heads that of a district.

questions.q: Each letter is given its position in the alphabet (A = 1, B = 2, and so on) and a word's value is the sum of its letters, so GOA = 7 + 15 + 1 = 23. What is the value of PANAJI?
Pointing to a woman, Rohan said, "She is the only daughter of my mother's father." How is the woman related to Rohan?
questions.why: His mother's father is his maternal grandfather. That man's only daughter is Rohan's mother.

questions.q: Priya is facing east. She turns 90 degrees clockwise, then 180 degrees, then 90 degrees anticlockwise. Which direction is she facing now?
questions.why: East, then clockwise to south, then about-turn to north, then anticlockwise to west.

questions.q: In a group of 60 candidates, 35 know Konkani, 30 know Marathi and 10 know neither language. How many know both?
questions.why: 50 candidates know at least one language. 35 + 30 - 50 = 15 know both.

questions.q: Milk and water are mixed in the ratio 7 : 3. How much water must be added to 10 litres of the mixture to make the ratio 7 : 5?
questions.why: 10 L has 7 L milk and 3 L water. For 7 : 5 water must be 5 L: add 2 L. GPSC CBRT, Jan 2026.

questions.q: Two ships on opposite sides of a 100 m lighthouse see its top at elevations of 30° and 45°. How far apart are the ships?
questions.why: Distances are 100√3 ≈ 173 m and 100 m; on opposite sides they add to about 273 m. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Statement: “Management should implement remote work to improve productivity.” Which assumption is implicit?
questions.why: The advice only makes sense if remote work does raise productivity. GPSC CBRT, Jan 2026.

questions.q: Find the odd set of letters:

questions.q: Wrist drop results from injury to the:
questions.why: The radial nerve supplies the wrist extensors; it is often injured in shaft-of-humerus fractures.

questions.q: Foot drop follows injury to the:
questions.why: It winds around the neck of the fibula and supplies the dorsiflexors.

questions.q: Claw hand is classically due to a lesion of the:
questions.why: Ulnar claw from paralysis of the interossei and medial lumbricals.

questions.q: The knee joint is an example of a:
questions.why: A synovial hinge with some rotation.

questions.q: The normal pacemaker of the heart is the:

questions.q: On the ECG, the QRS complex represents:
questions.why: P = atrial depolarisation, T = ventricular repolarisation.

questions.q: The first heart sound is produced by closure of the:
questions.why: S1 marks the start of ventricular systole.

questions.q: Mean arterial pressure is approximately:
questions.why: Diastole lasts longer, so MAP sits nearer the diastolic value.

questions.q: The baroreceptors that regulate blood pressure are located mainly in the:
questions.why: Carotid and aortic bodies are chemoreceptors.

questions.q: The principal muscle of quiet inspiration is the:
questions.why: It provides most of the tidal volume.

questions.q: The volume of air remaining in the lungs after maximal expiration is the:
questions.why: About 1.2 litres; it cannot be measured by simple spirometry.

questions.q: The substance commonly used to measure glomerular filtration rate precisely is:
questions.why: Inulin is freely filtered and neither reabsorbed nor secreted; PAH measures renal plasma flow.

questions.q: Glucose is normally reabsorbed in the nephron mainly in the:
questions.why: Almost all filtered glucose is reabsorbed proximally.

questions.q: Antidiuretic hormone acts mainly on the:
questions.why: It inserts aquaporins and concentrates urine.

questions.q: Bile salts are mainly required for the digestion and absorption of:
questions.why: They emulsify fat and form micelles.

questions.q: Vitamin B12 is absorbed mainly in the:
questions.why: Bound to intrinsic factor.

questions.q: Intrinsic factor is secreted by the:
questions.why: Parietal cells also secrete HCl.

questions.q: Which hormone is secreted by the posterior pituitary?
questions.why: Oxytocin and ADH are made in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary.

questions.q: A rise in thyroxine level suppresses TSH secretion. This is an example of:
questions.why: Classic endocrine negative feedback.

questions.q: Normal pH of arterial blood is:
questions.why: Below 7.35 is acidaemia; above 7.45 alkalaemia.

questions.q: The main extracellular cation is:
questions.why: Potassium is the main intracellular cation.

questions.q: Which lipoprotein is called 'good cholesterol'?
questions.why: HDL carries cholesterol back to the liver.

questions.q: The hormone that lowers blood glucose is:
questions.why: The others raise blood glucose.
